A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KGE-MoS work despite the changed title and format. All pages, including appendices, are readable, and retained methods, equations, figures and tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, mixture ablations, empirical matrix ranks and computational measurements in Section 6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original graph-ordering analyses, ablations, comparator results, computational measurements and sign-reconstruction results.

M1.justification: The core softmax mixture, shared entity embeddings, projections and regularization remain unchanged. v3 adds a sigmoid-mixture adaptation for sign reconstruction (Equation 14) and an auxiliary RCM entity-ordering procedure for tightening dimensional bounds (Appendix B).

E1.justification: All five datasets are retained, but empirical task coverage expands to binary triple classification through sign reconstruction on ogbl-biokg (Appendix F.5, Table 20). v2 discussed this third theoretical objective without evaluating it; v3 adds training with negative labels and evaluation of per-triple decisions.

E2.justification: The principal baseline set remains, but Table 18 adds TransE and RotatE against DISTMULT-MOS on ogbl-biokg, extending comparisons beyond linear-decoder families. COMPLEX and COMPLEX-MOS also join the previously DISTMULT-only mixture-count comparison in Table 4. NBFNet and ensembles are discussed, not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Existing splits, filtered MRR/NLL, embedding sizes and main training schedules are retained. Added protocols include treating unseen triples as negatives for sign reconstruction with AUROC/AP/F1, controlling projection depth, and profiling ConcatMLP across hidden widths and batch configurations (Appendices F.4.5, F.4.7 and F.5).

E4.justification: v3 extends the mixture-count ablation to COMPLEX, adds one-versus-two-layer projection controls, tests RCM ordering to tighten graph bounds, and adds whole-training and ConcatMLP resource analyses. These substantially expand evidence about mixture versus projection benefits, graph structure and computational limitations.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three runs with different initializations, report standard deviations and use paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests at p < 0.05. The original mixture-ablation uncertainties move to v3 Table 16, which extends the same reporting practice to COMPLEX. No increased run count or new statistical procedure is reported.

E6.justification: The original result tables retain their numerical values. v3 adds RCM bounds, ablation and comparator scores, resource measurements and sign-reconstruction outcomes; for example, Table 20 reports DISTMULT/DISTMULT-MOS AUROC of .891/.985. A new Section 5 claim of rank 14,501 at d=200, K=4 conflicts with the retained Table 7 value of 3,651.

T1.justification: v3 adds graph-specific RR/SR necessary bounds, DR universality and support-specific-threshold proofs. Theorem 4.1 is refined into a sign-change formulation with block-ordering bounds. New derivations address bilinear guarantees, Euclidean scoring and ensembles in Appendices E.2, F.4.6 and G, substantially extending v2's mathematical treatment.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions now foreground necessary dimensional bounds for both universality and graph-specific realisability across linear-decoder KGEs, explicitly emphasizing data-fitting expressivity. This expands v2's central contribution of identifying bottlenecks and providing a sufficient connectivity bound. The principal KGE-MoS performance claim is retained.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning neural versus bilinear realisability, learning constructive factorizations, projection capacity, ConcatMLP memory requirements and sign-reconstruction class imbalance. v2's explicit warning about untested million-scale graphs disappears, while its encoder-representability and runtime limitations largely remain in other passages.

D1.justification: New details specify RCM co-occurrence construction using the most prolific 0.1% of query rows, cached object projections for ConcatMLP, and exact 30-epoch training times. These document the added analyses. Main hyperparameters, A10 hardware and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against Wang et al. (2018)'s bilinear bounds and ensembles, supported by new Appendices E.2 and G. It adds research on rounding rank, RCM, cosine-based KGEs and embedding retrieval, and revises discussion of geometric models and NBFNet. Numerous other citation-year changes are publication updates to existing works.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, with extensive rewrites of the abstract, introduction and theoretical narrative. It introduces LD-KGE terminology, reorganizes background and proofs around universality/realisability, expands related-work discussion and adds an Impact Statement. These exceed localized wording edits.

P2.justification: The entire document changes from single-column to two-column layout, relocating and resizing retained displays. Figure 4's labels, arrangement and caption are revised; the connectivity table gains RCM columns; mixture-ablation displays are expanded and redistributed. New tables present theoretical bounds, resource measurements, additional comparisons and sign-reconstruction results.

improvement.justification: The added COMPLEX and projection-depth controls better distinguish projection-capacity gains from mixing, while explicit realisability bounds and measured RCM refinements strengthen the theory's practical connection. These benefits are tempered by new errors: Section 5's rank claim contradicts Table 7, and Appendix E.2 unjustifiably converts the sign/rounding-rank inequality into an equality. With the original method and benchmark evidence intact, the net quality gain is limited.
